title: The Abolitionists
objective: After this level you can explain how Frederick Douglass, William Lloyd Garrison and others argued to end slavery, and why many Northerners opposed them.
summary: Garrison’s Liberator (1831) demanded immediate emancipation; Douglass’s Narrative (1845) answered doubters. Many Northerners objected, and a mob killed Elijah Lovejoy.

cards.headline: Ending slavery was not a popular cause, even in the North.
cards.body: The abolitionists had printing presses, newspapers and one extraordinary witness. They also had enemies in Northern towns. Why?

cards.headline: "I will be heard"
cards.body: On January 1, 1831, William Lloyd Garrison published the first issue of The Liberator. He demanded immediate emancipation, not a slow phase-out, and promised in capital letters: "I WILL BE HEARD." In 1833 he helped organize the American Anti-Slavery Society.

cards.headline: A witness who had lived it
cards.body: Frederick Douglass escaped slavery in 1838 disguised as a sailor. Some people doubted he had ever been enslaved. So in 1845 he published his Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, partly to answer those doubters. In 1847 he launched his own newspaper, The North Star, despite objections from Garrison and others.

cards.headline: Why many Northerners objected
cards.body: Many Northerners distrusted abolitionists, fearing they threatened harmony between North and South. Critics argued the Constitution left slavery to each state. Demanding immediate emancipation was unpopular even among many Northerners who disliked slavery. Mobs destroyed Elijah Lovejoy’s antislavery press several times, and on November 7, 1837, a mob in Alton, Illinois, killed him as he defended it.

cards.headline: The abolitionists
learned: Many Northerners feared abolitionists would divide the nation
A mob killed Elijah Lovejoy in 1837

questions.prompt: What did William Lloyd Garrison’s Liberator demand?

options.label: Sending freed people to Africa
options.rationale: Garrison demanded emancipation now, in the United States.

options.label: A new compromise line
options.rationale: He wanted slavery ended, not divided.

questions.explanation: From its first issue in 1831, The Liberator demanded immediate emancipation.

questions.prompt: Garrison, Douglass and Lovejoy all relied on the same weapon against slavery. What was it?

options.label: Lawsuits in the Supreme Court
options.rationale: That was the Cherokee strategy in Level 41.

options.label: Armed revolt
options.rationale: None of them led a revolt.

options.label: Seats in Congress
options.rationale: None of them sat in Congress in this story.

questions.explanation: The Liberator, The North Star and Lovejoy’s press: abolitionists fought with print.

questions.prompt: Why did many Northerners oppose the abolitionists?

options.label: They feared abolitionists threatened harmony between North and South
They believed abolitionists secretly wanted slavery to spread west
They linked abolitionists to the anti-Catholic Know-Nothings
options.rationale: The card makes no such link.

options.label: They blamed abolitionists for the Panic over the Erie Canal
options.rationale: The card says nothing about the canal.

questions.explanation: Many feared abolitionists threatened sectional harmony, and critics said the Constitution left slavery to the states.
